extracted.intended_audience: researchers considering applying for ERC grants (EU and non-EU), at various career stages
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance on the main ERC funding schemes (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced, Proof of Concept, Synergy) and practical resources to help researchers decide whether and how to apply. Includes eligibility pointers, key documents, contacts and explanatory videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Starting Grants eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 2-7 years of experience since the completion of their PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets early-career researchers. Applicants should demonstrate a scientific track record that indicates high potential and submit an excellent research proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Consolidator Grants eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 7-12 years of experience since completion of PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at researchers consolidating their independent careers. Applicants should have 7–12 years post-PhD, show strong promise in their track record, and present an excellent research proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Advanced Grants eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for active researchers with a track-record of significant research achievements in the last 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at established, leading researchers. The emphasis is on a demonstrable record of significant achievements over the previous decade.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Proof of Concept eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers who have already received an ERC grant for their frontier research project and now want to explore the commercial or societal potential of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-on funding for previous ERC grantees to explore commercialization or societal impact of an ERC-funded project. Applicants must be former ERC grant holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Synergy Grants eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for two to maximum four researchers working together and bringing different skills and resources to tackle ambitious research problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for small teams (2–4 PIs). Teams should be complementary, bring diverse skills and resources, and address highly ambitious, collaborative research challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional opportunities linked to ERC funding
rubrics_metrics.description: There are other initiatives linked to ERC funding. If you are not planning to apply for a grant, or it’s too early to, you may still be interested in these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for researchers who are not yet ready to apply or are exploring alternatives; check these initiatives as possible entry points or preparatory opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: National contact points as primary support
rubrics_metrics.description: These are some of the first people you should contact about your ERC application. There is one based in every EU and Associated Country, as well as in some countries outside Europe. They are designated to help applicants out in their own countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your national contact point early for country-specific guidance and support on ERC applications; they are an official local resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult frequently asked questions (FAQs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a question about your ERC application? Chances are you’re not alone. Throughout the years, we have collected some of the most frequently asked questions to guide you through the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FAQs to resolve common queries and understand typical applicant concerns before seeking further help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult key documents and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are considering applying, you'll have several key documents to refer to, like the Work Programme and the Information for Applicants. These highlight the specifics of the calls every year, as well as providing some useful information to think about before you embark on the process itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always read the Work Programme and Information for Applicants for the specific call year to learn eligibility details, call-specific rules, deadlines, and application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for non-EU researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a researcher from outside the EU and you wish to apply check out some of the things you should consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-EU applicants should review the specific considerations and potential constraints or requirements that apply to applicants based outside the EU/Associated Countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch the ERC step-by-step introductory video
rubrics_metrics.description: For a short introduction to ERC grants, watch our step-by-step video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise overview resource for applicants who want a quick orientation to the ERC schemes and application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the ERC Classes (5-part video series)
rubrics_metrics.description: This series of 5 explanatory videos will give you concrete information about the ERC application process, including frequently made mistakes, tips and rumours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the series to get detailed, practical guidance on common mistakes, tips for applications, and clarifications of common rumours about the ERC process.
